title: Degreewise finite-free affine Hom comparisons with arbitrary coefficients
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an affine open, $A=\Gamma(Y,U)$, and $K_\bullet$ a chain complex of $A$-modules in nonnegative degrees [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] whose terms are finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Write $T$ for associated sheafification transported from $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ to $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. There is a family $e_{q,N}:\mathcal{H}om(T(K_q),T(N))\simeq T(\operatorname{Hom}_A(K_q,N))$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], for every $q\geq0$ and every $A$-module $N$. It commutes with precomposition by $d_{q+1}:K_{q+1}\to K_q$ and with postcomposition by every $A$-linear map $g:N\to N\prime$. More precisely, precompose by $T(d_{q+1})$ then apply $e_{q+1,N}$ equals $e_{q,N}$ then $T$ of precomposition by $d_{q+1}$; and postcompose by $T(g)$ then apply $e_{q,N\prime}$ equals $e_{q,N}$ then $T$ of postcomposition by $g$. There is no freeness assumption on the coefficients, no differential sign, no extension of complexes, and no boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Obtain the natural forward comparison c for all module pairs, with rank-one components invertible.
The finite-basis inverse theorem makes each c(K_q,N) invertible, using freeness, finiteness and the additivity of the affine associated-sheaf functor.

Set e(q,N) to the inverse isomorphism of c(K_q,N). Cancel the invertible forward component from each desired square and rewrite by the precomposition or postcomposition naturality equation of c. This proves both identities for one family.

lean.statement:
theorem affine_finite_free_coefficient_comparisons
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.affineOpens)
    (K : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, U.1)) ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ q : ℕ, Module.Free Γ(Y, U.1) (K.X q))
    (hfinite : ∀ q : ℕ, Module.Finite Γ(Y, U.1) (K.X q)) :
    let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    ∃ e : ∀ (q : ℕ) (N : ModuleCat.{u} A),
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
          (T.obj (K.X q)) (T.obj N) ≅ T.obj (ModuleCat.of A (K.X q ⟶ N)),
      (∀ (q : ℕ) (N : ModuleCat.{u} A),
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
          (T.map (K.d (q + 1) q)) (𝟙 (T.obj N)) ≫ (e (q + 1) N).hom =
        (e q N).hom ≫ T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.leftComp A N (K.d (q + 1) q)))) ∧
      (∀ (q : ℕ) (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A) (g : N ⟶ N'),
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.1.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
          (𝟙 (T.obj (K.X q))) (T.map g) ≫ (e q N').hom =
        (e q N).hom ≫ T.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.rightComp A (K.X q) g)))
